basis: Congenital absence of teeth; teeth and impaired mastication belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Intellectual disability and skeletal anomalies define syndrome; heart defects ~40-50%, hearing loss ~50%. Oral and renal anomalies omitted at cap; small HPO samples do not establish prevalence.
Dysplastic glandular epithelial neoplasm arising in rectal mucosa.
Acute leukemia of mixed lineage involving blood and marrow; neither the FLT3 gene nor the erroneous connective-tissue ancestor establishes another organ.
Thymic epithelial tumor; thymus has no listed anatomical axis. It is not lymphoma or an immune-mediated disease; associated myasthenia and cytopenias are separate conditions.
Immune-mediated delayed hypersensitivity causing eczematous inflammation of light-exposed skin.
Congenital cerebral ventricular enlargement; supplied HPO annotations place structural iris coloboma and strabismus at 30-79%. Optic atrophy and hearing loss are only 1-4%.
Originally delineated through developmental delay, supporting a neurologic assignment. Phenotype remains uncertain; delay is annotated in only 5-29%, and no other organ damage is established.
Defining mandibulofacial skeletal malformation and congenital bilateral ptosis. Ear canal defects and hearing loss are reported, but their prevalence is unspecified.
Cholesterol emboli obstruct small arteries; direct ischemic renal injury occurs in ~50-80% of systemic cases. Common skin discoloration does not establish lasting skin damage.
Severe limb/craniofacial dysostosis; microtia 80-99%, CNS and cardiac malformations 30-79%. Palatal and lung abnormalities omitted at cap; renal defects only 5-29%.
Antibody-mediated neonatal thrombophilia causing vascular thrombosis. Site-specific infarctions vary; available information does not establish an additional organ above the threshold.
Female genital prolapse is primarily reproductive. Bladder displacement in some subtypes does not establish common intrinsic urinary organ damage across this umbrella.
EIF2B1-related degeneration of cerebral white matter. Blindness is annotated at 5-29%; ovarian insufficiency lacks evidence of ≥30% prevalence across all patients.
Generalized skeletal sclerosis and hyperostosis. Hearing impairment and facial palsy occur in only 5-29%; palatal bony exostoses do not establish gastrointestinal dysfunction.
Adult skeletal-muscle-lineage sarcoma, typically arising in deep soft tissues of the extremities.
Inherited melanin-production disorder defined by skin/hair hypopigmentation and ocular dysfunction; reduced visual acuity, nystagmus and iris transillumination occur in 9/9 reported patients.
Dental malposition with variable congenital tooth absence; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited disease of cardiac muscle. Extracardiac findings belong to particular subtypes and do not characterize most patients across the umbrella.
Defined by severe central nervous system dysfunction associated with hepatic failure or portosystemic shunting.
Defined by microangiopathic hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury from small-vessel thrombotic endothelial injury. Infection is not universal across subtypes.
Umbrella of iron handling disorders. Hepatic, hematologic and neurologic damage vary by subtype; no additional organ damage is established across most patients.
Partial 11q trisomy commonly causes developmental delay and intellectual disability. Cardiac, skeletal and other structural abnormalities vary with the duplicated interval.
Benign vascular neoplasm arising in the skin. Associated POEMS syndrome is a separate disease and does not justify additional axes.
Adipocytic sarcoma of limb soft tissues and subcutis; subcutaneous nodules are annotated at 80-99%. Gastrointestinal symptoms occur in only 5-29% and do not establish direct damage.
